findings.text: Memory escaping service transforms a bounded input extent into a bounded output extent under caller supplied class flags and an optional selection set, processing every input byte in order and emitting either a direct copy or an encoded form, always counting the full logical output length even when the destination is too small and returning that count.

Byte search services scan a terminated sequence forward for a wanted value, one reporting absence with a null result and the other reporting the terminator position itself, stopping at the first match or at termination.

Span measurement services compute a leading run length over a terminated sequence, one counting while bytes belong to an accepted set and the other counting while bytes avoid a rejected set, stopping at termination or the first disqualifying byte and reporting the run length.

Unbounded duplication service copies a terminated sequence including its terminator into caller provided storage and reports the destination origin, enforcing no length limit itself so caller reserve determines safety.

Escaped memory print extension honors width driven length where zero yields no output and negative yields a single unit, validates the source pointer before use, accumulates escape classes from trailing option letters with fallback to a default nonprintable any set when none are given, then delegates to the general escaping service using remaining buffer space and advances by the full encoded length.

Escape option scanning consumes consecutive recognized letters starting after the introducer where letters a c h n o p and s select any special hex null octal nonprintable and space classes respectively, stopping at the first unrecognized letter and falling back to a default nonprintable any set when no class was selected.

Escaping precedence first considers dictionary membership and printable or ascii fast passes, then whitespace symbolic and null encodings, with octal and hexadecimal encodings last and direct copy as final fallback, where an append modifier changes how dictionary membership interacts with the fast passes.

Whitespace handling converts newline carriage return tab vertical tab and form feed into backslash plus respective letters n r t v and f and declines other bytes, symbolic handling converts backslash bell escape and quote into backslash plus backslash a e and quote respectively and declines others, null handling converts only zero into backslash zero, octal handling always emits backslash plus three octal digits, hex handling always emits backslash x plus two hex digits, and passthrough always emits the byte unchanged.

Nested format extension validates its descriptor pointer, duplicates the caller variadic state, formats the embedded template into remaining buffer space, releases the duplicate, and returns the advanced position.

Identifier extension validates its source pointer, selects byte order and letter case from an option letter where capital L and lowercase l choose GUID order with upper and lower case respectively and capital B chooses standard order with upper case defaulting otherwise to standard lower, renders 16 bytes as paired hex digits with dashes after byte indices 3 5 7 and 9, terminates the intermediate form, then emits under caller width rules.

Network feature extension validates its source pointer, accepts only letter capital F in second position for feature sets and otherwise yields an error placeholder, then renders the numeric value as a sized hexadecimal form.

Four character code extension requires letter c in second position and otherwise yields an error placeholder, validates its source pointer, fetches an unaligned value, interprets third position letter h as host with optional capital R in fourth position requesting reversal and letters l b and c as little big and pixel respectively with other values yielding an error placeholder, renders 4 bytes most significant first as printable ascii or dots using a byte swapped value with the high bit cleared in pixel mode, appends big versus little endian wording for pixel mode based on the high bit with blank separators and always appends a blank plus parenthesized hexadecimal of the possibly converted original.

Address value extension validates its source pointer, interprets letter d as DMA width and any other including p as physical width, then renders the referenced numeric value as a sized hexadecimal form.

Time dispatcher validates its pointer and routes letters capital R S and T to calendar versus timespec versus seconds forms respectively, yielding an error placeholder for other letters, with timespec supporting a raw seconds variant selected by letter p in the next position and otherwise combining calendar plus fractional nanoseconds.

Calendar option scanning first checks for letter d meaning date only and letter t meaning time only defaulting to both, then consumes consecutive letters r meaning raw numbers and s meaning blank joiner versus default standards joiner, stopping at the first unrecognized letter, then emits requested parts in date then time order.

Date emission uses 4 digit year followed by 2 digit month and day joined by dashes, time emission uses 2 digit hour minute and second joined by colons, non raw mode adds 1900 to year and 1 to month while raw mode uses stored values directly, and seconds conversion builds a calendar record with zero daylight flag before delegating to calendar rendering.
Timespec rendering emits seconds either as plain decimal or as calendar form according to a following option letter, always follows with a dot, then emits nanoseconds as 9 digit zero padded decimal.

Clock extension reports an error placeholder when clock support is disabled at build time, otherwise validates its pointer and then either renders the associated name under caller width rules or renders an identifier form depending on common clock configuration.

Flag rendering validates its pointer and dispatches letters p v and g to page versus virtual memory versus allocation families respectively with an error placeholder otherwise, emits known bits as names joined by vertical bars while clearing consumed bits and rendering leftovers numerically, and for pages prefixes a numeric value plus parenthesized named bits and field assignments.

Device tree extension requires leading capital F and firmware extension requires leading w, both validate pointers and configuration gates, interpret subsequent letters f n p capital P capital F c and capital C as full path short name numeric handle path flag word major compatible and full compatible respectively with firmware accepting capital P for name and defaulting to full path, join multiple device selections with colons, and apply caller width rules only after composing the full intermediate result.

Device node selector handling defaults to full name when no recognized selector is present, otherwise iterates over the longest leading run of recognized selectors from the set f n p capital P capital F c and capital C, inserting a separator between passes and leaving width handling until the end.

Resource dispatcher chooses range rendering for leading letters r a and otherwise resource rendering, resource rendering validates its pointer and labels the kind from flag bits among input output memory interrupt DMA bus or unknown, shows either a size value when decode plus unset is present or a start to end span otherwise, appends decoded attributes or raw flag numerals according to whether the leading letter is capital R, and range rendering shows a bracketed labeled span with range tag and start to end values, both via bounded intermediates.

Resource hexadecimal widths are fixed at 6 for input output kinds and 10 for memory kinds, with bus kinds using 2, and string label fields use negative width plus precision 10 with left justification.

Resource scratch sizing sets the numeric span from twice the address size plus 4, the flag scratch from twice the flag storage size, and decoded and raw wording from their longest literal forms, combined to bound the largest possible composed line.

Width and precision setters clamp caller values into implementation limits, preserving sign for width and flooring at 0 for precision, and emit a one time diagnostic when the requested value exceeds the allowed range.

Formatting helpers never write past the supplied end yet always advance the return pointer by the full logical length including truncated portions, querying remaining space before each write and counting unwritten bytes toward the total, so callers observe truncated output but correct advancement.

Most extensions validate pointers through a common helper before dereference and return early on failure, while low level duplication and search helpers assume valid terminated inputs and the former can overrun its destination if the caller reserve is insufficient.

Format specification records as observed carry at least a width and a precision plus a numeric base and formatting flags, with width driving output length and truncation and precision limiting string portions, though the full definition is not present in these fragments.

Calendar records as observed expose second minute hour day month year weekday yearday and daylight fields, resource records expose start end and flag bits, range records expose start and end, and flag tables expose mask plus name pairs, though complete layouts are not present here.
Span helper emits a single value when start equals end and otherwise emits start dash end, preserving caller numeric formatting choices for both endpoints.

Full name composition walks from root depth down to the target, acquiring references only for ancestor handles and releasing each after use while leaving the target reference untouched, emitting prefix plus name at each level.

Page field rendering skips entries with zero width, otherwise emits each field name followed by equals and the extracted bitfield value under per field formatting, joining multiple fields and the main flag names with vertical bars inside parentheses after a leading numeric value.

Device flag word emits 4 positions in order dynamic detached populated and populated bus using letters capital D lowercase d capital P and capital B respectively when set and dashes otherwise, terminated before emission.
Short name rendering truncates at the first at sign to remove unit addressing, preserving an incoming precision limit across the operation by restoring it afterwards.
Path rendering substitutes a solitary slash when the retrieved name has at most 1 character, otherwise emitting the retrieved name directly.
Resource kind labels use 3 letter abbreviations padded to 4 characters with trailing blanks for known kinds and question marks for unknown, where unknown also disables decoded attribute appending.

Decoded mode appends space separated words 64bit pref window and disabled in that fixed order when the corresponding flag bits are set, while non decoded mode instead appends flag numerals with a label and separators.
